title: Redwood technical deep dive - Dedicated vs Hosted (KV cache, batching, quantization, VPC)
summary: Customer (OptiRetail) and Redwood team dug into tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated for high-throughput recommendation inference. Key concerns: isolation/noisy neighbors, per-token latency p95, KV cache hit rates for session-based recs, batching strategies and quantization impact on quality, and VPC/on-prem constraints for PII. Agreed next steps: share SLO doc, run a 2-week dedicated pilot + benchmark with customer's sample workload, and propose batching/quant profiles.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Omar Rahman (Redwood Solutions), Mark Johnson (OptiRetail Head of ML), Priya Singh (OptiRetail Infra), Ellen Park (OptiRetail Security)
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/docs/dedicated-slos.pdf, https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/kv-cache-batching.xlsx

[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: we wanted to walk through dedicated vs hosted for your recommender pipelines, focus on KV cache, batching, quant, and the vpc/on-prem constraints you mentioned.
[00:25] Mark Johnson: thanks Liam, yeah high level question for context - we do real-time personalization at scale, peak throughput is ~6k reqs/s, and p95 token latency target is around 120ms.
[00:40] Priya Singh: and we have strict data residency + some PII that needs to remain inside our vpc, so private deployment is a hard ask for parts of the workload.
[00:55] Sofia Martinez: cool, that helps. just to flag - some terms may come out a bit off, I might say "Redwood Dedicat" or "kv cash" in the transcript, sorry in advance.
[01:10] Omar Rahman: right, and I'll jump in on the orchestration side. can you share your typical sequence lengths and model family?
[01:22] Mark Johnson: sequences for recommendation sessions are short, 16-64 tokens, avg 28. model is a 7B LLM we fine-tuned for ranking, currently running on g4-like infra.
[01:35] Sofia Martinez: good - short sequences play nicely with KV cache because we can cache prefix embeddings across session history. what's your cache hit rate today?
[01:48] Priya Singh: roughly 45% hit rate across our sessions, higher for logged-in users. we'd love to push that up to 70% with smarter routing/caching.
[02:05] Liam Chen: perfect. high-level on dedicated vs hosted: Hosted gives fastest onboarding and auto-scaling, but you're sharing pools so in peak events you may see noisy neighbor variance. Dedicated reserves GPU pools for you - isolation and throughput guarantees, but comes with reserved commit and provisioning lead time.
[02:30] Mark Johnson: noise is our big worry. last holiday spike we saw p95 jump to 450ms locally - cost was unbounded. can dedicated help us meet that 120ms p95 target reliably?
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: yes, dedicated lets us size the pool to target p95 under your peak throughput. we plan capacity with a combination of baseline reserved instances and burst capacity. we can set SLOs in the Dedicated contract and back it with an SLA. I'll share the dedicated SLO doc after this call (see link).
[03:05] Ellen Park: on security, how does the private deployment differ? we need KMS integration and audit logs, plus SSO for control plane.
[03:20] Liam Chen: private gives you a customer-controlled VPC and optional on-prem. KMS/HSM integration and audit logs are supported; control plane is private. For hosted, we still provide encrypted-at-rest, SOC2 controls, and customer-tenant separation, but no VPC peering.
[03:40] Priya Singh: ok. if we do Dedicated but not fully private control plane, can we still enforce VPC peering or private networking?
[03:52] Sofia Martinez: yes - Redwood Dedicated can be deployed into a customer's VPC for network isolation. we call that "Dedicated in VPC" in the doc, it gives most of the isolation benefits without the full on-prem package.
[04:10] Mark Johnson: great. back to performance - can you explain how KV cache and batching interact? for short sequences does batching introduce extra latency?
[04:25] Sofia Martinez: good question. batching improves throughput and lowers cost per token, but it can add small queuing latency. our runtime dynamically adjusts batch windows: for low-latency SLOs we use micro-batching (1-4 requests) with lower wait windows, for throughput targets we increase batch size which increases per-request latency slightly. KV cache reduces tokens to compute by reusing cached keys/values, so effective tokens per request drop which reduces compute and can reduce the need for large batching.
[04:55] Mark Johnson: so if we can increase KV hit from 45% to 70% we might keep micro-batches and still hit throughput SLOs?
[05:05] Sofia Martinez: exactly. the math roughly: effective tokens = raw_tokens * (1 - kv_hit). higher kv_hit reduces GPU time and keeps latency low even at higher qps.
[05:18] Omar Rahman: and on noisy neighbor - Dedicated gives you fixed GPU capacity so your batch latency variance is much lower. hosted will have autoscaling but noisy neighbor can impact tail latencies. we also support fallback routing to model variants when a node is hot.
[05:35] Priya Singh: what about quantization? we tried 4-bit to save cost but saw ranking quality drop a bit. is there a recommended profile for 7B rankers?
[05:50] Sofia Martinez: we recommend mixed approach: keep the critical ranking head in fp16 or 8-bit quant, quantize attention/matrix multiplies to 4-bit where quality is tolerant. we have Per-Layer Quant profiles and will run a quality regression on your eval set. typical impact for 7B is low if we tune per-layer and do calibration.
[06:15] Mark Johnson: can you run that with our eval set? we care about nerfing any drop in NDCG@10 more than token latency.
[06:25] Liam Chen: yes - next steps cover that: Priya to share evals + prompts and Sofia to run quant + batching sensitivity tests.
[06:38] Mark Johnson: we also need throughput guarantees - what's the format of those SLOs? p95 latency, availability?
[06:48] Liam Chen: standard SLOs we offer: p50/p95/p99 token latencies, availability SLA, and a throughput baseline (requests/sec) for Dedicated. The doc linked has examples and the penalty/credits for missing SLA. We'll send the version keyed to your peak qps.
[07:05] Ellen Park: and audit logs - is there plaintext PII recorded in logs, how do you redact?
[07:14] Omar Rahman: we provide configurable log redaction and PII filters; for Private/VPC we can keep logs inside your infra or push to your SIEM.
[07:28] Priya Singh: curious about caching: do you shard KV cache per-tenant? and eviction policies?
[07:36] Sofia Martinez: yes, cache is sharded by tenant/session id in dedicated deployments; eviction uses LRU with configurable TTLs. we can pin hot prefixes for frequently-seen user sequences to increase hit rate.
[07:52] Mark Johnson: earlier you mentioned prefix caching - can you give an example for our recs flow?
[07:58] Sofia Martinez: imagine recurrent session of user browsing - first N tokens form prefix context; we store the KV for that prefix. subsequent requests only compute new tokens. For us it's transparent: the runtime handles prefix matching and returns cached KV hits, you get fewer tokens computed end-to-end.
[08:18] Priya Singh: latency numbers - can you share realistic p95 with Dedicated sized for our 6k rps and 28 token avg?
[08:28] Sofia Martinez: ballpark, with Dedicated and conservative micro-batching and 70% KV hit, p95 token latency ~80-110ms depending on model and GPU type. On hosted shared pools during heavy contention we've seen p95 spike >300-400ms.
[08:45] Mark Johnson: what's the fallback if a dedicated node fails? do requests fall back to hosted?
[08:52] Liam Chen: we support multi-tier routing: primary to Dedicated, fallback to compatible Hosted model variant if dedicated capacity is temporarily down. that can be configured per-route and is often used to prevent 5xxs during maintenance.
[09:05] Ellen Park: ok that's useful. about data residency, if we use dedicated in VPC, are audit logs still exported to Redwood telemetry?
[09:15] Omar Rahman: by default minimal telemetry is sent for health, but we can turn off telemetry and route logs to your SIEM in VPC deployments. full private control plane option has no telemetry out.
[09:30] Mark Johnson: cost question: dedicated reservation vs hosted- do you have a model to compare cost per qps? we need to justify the commit.
[09:40] Liam Chen: yes we'll provide a cost model tied to your expected qps and KV hit improvements. often customers that can push KV hit above ~60% and have stable baselines prefer Dedicated because unit cost drops and tail latency is predictable, but if you have spiky and unpredictable load hosted lowers upfront commitment.
[10:05] Priya Singh: what about GPU types and kernel selection - can we pick A100 vs H100?
[10:15] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated lets you choose compatible GPU families; kernel selection is handled by our runtime which will pick optimized kernels per architecture. if you need explicit H100, we'll size the pool accordingly (pricing differs).
[10:30] Mark Johnson: any notes about partitioning traffic across regions? we will have EU and NA tenants.
[10:38] Omar Rahman: smart routing supports region-based routing and per-tenant pinning. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region clusters, otherwise we can set data routing policies.
[10:50] Mark Johnson: can you describe how you benchmarked KV cache + batching - what metrics should we expect to see in the spreadsheet?
[10:58] Sofia Martinez: we'll run tests varying qps, batch windows, and kv hit rates. key metrics: tokens/sec, GPU util, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV hit rate, and quality delta (NDCG) against eval set for quantized models. 
[11:18] Priya Singh: for the pilot, how long should bench run be to be meaningful?
[11:24] Liam Chen: a two-week pilot with representative peak windows is ideal to capture diurnal patterns and tail events. one-off runs are useful but don't capture spikes/noise.
[11:34] Mark Johnson: makes sense. anything else on tooling or monitoring?
[11:40] Sofia Martinez: Redwood Console gives per-route token-level cost and tracing. you can also instrument custom traces for a sample of requests and tie regressions to prompt sets. we can provision an eval dashboard for your pilot.
[11:55] Priya Singh: one operational concern: during a hot fix we need to roll back model quickly. how are rollouts handled in Dedicated?
[12:05] Omar Rahman: rollouts are canary/A-B with automatic rollback on regressions. Dedicated supports gradual traffic shifts across your reserved nodes.
[12:18] Mark Johnson: we have some internal security audits - any pre-approved language for our procurement?
[12:25] Liam Chen: procurement/legal packet will be sent by our deals team - we can include SOC2/ISO attestation and tailored data processing addendum.
[12:36] Ellen Park: thanks. small transcribe artifact: someone said "kv cash" earlier - noted :)
[12:42] Liam Chen: wrap up - agreed next steps and action owners, we'll send SLO doc and pricing. Sofia will run quant + batching sims once Priya shares prompt corpora. schedule pilot for week of 2026-03-08.
[12:58] Mark Johnson: sounds good, thanks team.
[13:05] Priya Singh: thank you. we'll get the samples over by Friday.
[13:10] Liam Chen: great, meeting end.

End of transcript

Notes on transcription quality: medium - occasional mis-labels and minor word errors (e.g., "Redwood Dedicat", "kv cash").

Recap (verbatim):
- Primary ask: predictable p95 under 120ms at ~6k rps for 28-token average.
- Solution direction: Redwood Dedicated in VPC with reserved baseline + burst, KV cache tuning to hit 70%+, micro-batching, and conservative quantization profile with per-layer calibration.
- Next steps: share SLO doc, run quantization/ batching experiments on customer eval set, provision pilot, share pricing and legal packet.
